name: Urubú-Kaapor Sign Language
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Sign language (Kakumasu 1968 describes the sign system); no word-stress description exists or applies

sources.citation: Godoy e Silva, Gustavo de. 2022. Língua de sinais, gestos e os perigos das cores: o caso ka'apor. LIAMES 22: e022012, 1-24. doi:10.20396/liames.v22i00.8667939
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; colour signs and gestures. Its reference list gives the ELAR deposit Aniz & Godoy 2020 and Godoy 2020a thesis (PPGAS/UFRJ).

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page and JSON for urub1243 (Godoy 2020; Kakumasu 2004, 1968, 1966; Brito 1985/1984; Ferreira 2010; Ethnologue 2009); English Wikipedia 'Kaʼapor Sign Language'
sources.note: Glottolog tags all refs as wordlist-or-less except Godoy 2020 ('phonology or text'); Wikipedia summarises OSV order, time-line and non-manual marking, nothing on prosody.

sources.citation: Godoy, Gustavo. 2020. É o tempo dos gestos nos sinais. Revista Linguíʃtica 16(3): 60-102. doi:10.31513/linguistica.2020.v16n3a36942
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; describes temporal reference in LSK with primary data (sign ANTIGAMENTE made with a 'movimento tenso' plus intensifying facial expression, p. ~72). Notes (fn. 3) that a study of LSK is Godoy 2020a (the thesis).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-059 (submitted by Alan Vogel with James Kakumasu, SIL-Brazil): rename [uks] to Kaapor Sign Language
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Naming request only; no linguistic description.

sources.citation: Ferreira Brito, Lucinda. 1984. Similarities & differences in two Brazilian sign languages. Sign Language Studies 42: 45-56. doi:10.1353/sls.1984.0003
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. Sociolinguistic and lexical comparison of UKSL and São Paulo SL; pp. 53-54 note that intensification can be carried by 'a stronger movement' of the sign and suggests comparing this 'visual contour' with 'the intonational contour of the same expressions in spoken languages' (about intensification, not stress placement).
